title: Keeping whitespace the compiler would remove

questions.stem: Per this page, how is trailing whitespace preserved inside a text block?

options.text: Place the closing delimiter on the line below
options.says: The page says trailing whitespace is stripped from each line by default; where the closing delimiter sits only changes the indentation and the final newline.

options.text: Call stripIndent() on the value afterwards
options.says: The page says stripIndent() applies the same algorithm as the compiler, which removes trailing whitespace rather than keeping it.

options.text: Write the \s escape as the line's last character
options.says: The page says the \s escape preserves trailing whitespace: the spaces before it are no longer at the end of the line.

questions.stem: Per this page, why do blank lines take no part in the smallest-indentation calculation?

options.text: A blank line with no spaces would otherwise force the minimum to zero
options.says: The page says a blank line with zero leading spaces would make every other line keep its source indentation, and editors often strip such lines.

options.text: A blank line is removed from the value before the minimum is found
options.says: The page says blank lines stay in the value as empty lines; they are only left out of the calculation.

options.text: A blank line always carries the same indentation as the line above
options.says: The page says editors handle whitespace on blank lines differently, so a blank line may carry any amount of it, or none.
